definition: set of one or more Samples or SampleCollections; collections may be nested.
original_axiom: subClassOf bfo:ObjectAggregate and (bfo:has_member_part some (sosa:Sample or sosa:SampleCollection))
corrected_axiom: sosa:SampleCollection rdfs:subClassOf obo:BFO_0000002 , [ a owl:Restriction ; owl:onProperty obo:BFO_0000178 ; owl:someValuesFrom [ a owl:Class ; owl:unionOf ( sosa:Sample sosa:SampleCollection ) ] ] ; rdfs:comment "Retyped from bfo:ObjectAggregate + has_member_part (both material) to bfo:Continuant + has_continuant_part: SOSA 2023 de-materialised sosa:Sample, and has_member_part (material to material) would re-impose materiality on member samples and drive any immaterial (e.g. spatial) sample to owl:Nothing. See Decisions needed."@en .
external_notes: SampleCollection is the only *Collection class in SOSA whose members are continuants rather than occurrents, and it is therefore modeled as a bfo:ObjectAggregate rather than a bfo:Process. Samples are physical (or spatial, or statistical) subsets of features of interest — they are things, not happenings — so aggregating them yields an object aggregate in BFO's sense. The parthood uses bfo:has_member_part (a specialization of bfo:has_continuant_part specifically for member-parthood of ObjectAggregates) rather than plain has_continuant_part, because this more precisely captures that Samples are member-objects of the aggregate rather than arbitrary spatial or fiat parts of a larger continuant. The four process-flavored collections use plain bfo:has_occurrent_part because BFO 2020 does not provide a parallel "member occurrent part" construct for processes. Note especially the contrast with sosa:SamplingCollection, which is a collection of sampling events (occurrents) and is therefore a bfo:Process — the distinction between "a collection of sampling acts" and "a collection of the samples those acts produced" is ontologically significant and is carried by this occurrent/continuant split. The axiom uses only a some-restriction on bfo:has_member_part and deliberately omits an only-restriction. Even though bfo:has_member_part is narrower than plain continuant parthood, an only-restriction is still risky here because member-parthood interacts with the continuant-parthood hierarchy, and a Sample has its own continuant parts (mineral grains in a rock sample, cells in a blood sample) that should not be forced to be Samples themselves. The homogeneity of direct collection members is enforced by the SHACL shape on sosa:hasMember (see Common OPs: sosa:hasMember). Note the terminological distinction: "SOSA member" refers to the sosa:hasMember relation; "BFO member-part" is the mereological relation between an ObjectAggregate and its member-objects. These two concepts are intentionally decoupled. The parthood of at least one member is asserted at the class level rather than through sosa:hasMember, because sosa:hasMember carries no parthood sub-property assertion (see Common OPs: sosa:hasMember). This row and the hasMember row work as a pair: the class carries the BFO parthood entailment where it is well-defined, the property carries the uniform SOSA collection-membership semantics, and SHACL shapes on hasMember validate member types per collection class.

The homogeneity of direct collection members is a constraint on direct sosa:hasMember edges, not on deep BFO occurrent parthood, and is enforced by the SHACL shape on sosa:hasMember (see Common OPs: sosa:hasMember). Note the terminological distinction: "SOSA member" refers to the sosa:hasMember relation; "BFO occurrent part" is the mereological relation that holds transitively. These are intentionally decoupled. The parthood of at least one member is asserted at the class level rather than through sosa:hasMember, because sosa:hasMember carries no parthood sub-property assertion (see Common OPs: sosa:hasMember). This row and the hasMember row work as a pair.

Note: as of CCO 2.2 cco:Sensor (ont00000569) is defined as 'A Material Entity that bears a Sensor Function or Sensor Role' (Sensor Function ont00001241, Sensor Role ont00002073), matching the issue-429 reading; the residual caveat is that a non-material software or simulation sensor still falls outside a Material-Entity cco:Sensor."@en .

Those conditions coincide - bearing a Sensor Function/Role is what it is to be realized as the sensing agent - so full equivalence holds rather than a one-way subclass. definition: link from a Collection to an Execution or Sample or Collection of these that is part of it

Member-type homogeneity is validated in the SHACL layer."@en .
external_notes: sosa:hasMember is declared as a bare object property with no BFO parthood sub-property assertion. The parthood semantics of collection membership are carried at the class level on each Collection class rather than on this property, because BFO 2020's continuant and occurrent parthood relations have disjoint domains and a single uniform member-relation cannot be a sub-property of both without rendering its arguments unsatisfiable. OWL 2 DL provides no disjunctive or domain-conditional sub-property construct that would let one property route to has_occurrent_part when the collection is process-flavored and to has_continuant_part (or has_member_part) when the collection is a SampleCollection. By declining to commit hasMember to any parthood reading, the property remains usable uniformly across all five SOSA collection types without forcing contradictory BFO classification on its arguments. This also honors the spec's own framing: SOSA 2023 §5.3.6 uses set-membership language for collections, and the OMS and OBOE alignment modules gloss hasMember as collection membership rather than parthood, so the non-parthood reading matches upstream intent. SHACL shapes on each Collection class (see SHACL column) validate that members are of the correct type per collection, which restores the integrity checking that the dropped sub-property axioms would have provided, without the unsatisfiability. A downstream profile that wants a generic part-whole reading of hasMember can override this row by asserting a custom parthood sub-property axiom scoped to its own collection classes.

external_notes: sosa:isMemberOf is declared as a bare object property whose only axiom is the inverse relationship to sosa:hasMember. Like hasMember, it carries no BFO parthood sub-property assertion, for the same reason: BFO 2020's continuant and occurrent parthood relations have disjoint domains, and a single uniform member-relation cannot be a sub-property of both without rendering its arguments unsatisfiable. By declining to commit isMemberOf to any parthood reading, the property remains usable uniformly across all five SOSA collection types (ObservationCollection, ActuationCollection, SamplingCollection, ExecutionCollection, SampleCollection). The inverse axiom to sosa:hasMember preserves bidirectional navigation at the SOSA level, which is the primary use case in queries and data authoring. SHACL shapes that validate member types are attached to sosa:hasMember (see Common OPs: sosa:hasMember); no additional shapes are needed on isMemberOf because the constraints are equivalent via the inverse relationship, and SHACL engines will apply them correctly regardless of which direction the data is authored in. Note the terminological distinction: "SOSA member" refers to collection membership via sosa:hasMember / sosa:isMemberOf; "BFO part" refers to bfo:has_occurrent_part or bfo:has_member_part asserted at the class level on each Collection. These two concepts are intentionally decoupled in this workbook — see sosa:hasMember on Common OPs for the full rationale.

definition: Relation between a System and its Operating Conditions, modelled as ObservationCollection (or Observation) describing conditions under which the System can operate. A short but extensible list of sub-classes of OperatingConditions is provided in SSN-System, such as normal operating conditions, suboptimal conditions, and survivable conditions.
corrected_axiom: sosa:hasOperatingConditions a owl:ObjectProperty ; rdfs:domain sosa:System ; rdfs:range sosa:OperatingConditions ; rdfs:comment "The workbook super-chain (bearer_of o inverse(is_about)) is not OWL 2 DL (anonymous chain-bearing property in the super position of subPropertyOf). The intended constraint — the operating-conditions Observation is about a specifically dependent continuant the System bears — is moved to the SHACL layer. Range narrowed to sosa:OperatingConditions to differentiate this property from sosa:hasSystemCapability."@en .
external_notes: sosa:hasOperatingConditions links a sosa:System to a sosa:ObservationCollection or sosa:Observation because the operating conditions are expressed as observed values of environmental properties. This is consistent with the broader SOSA pattern of using observations to describe system state and context. The range is a union because a single sosa:Observation suffices for simple cases while a sosa:ObservationCollection is needed for multi-dimensional condition descriptions. [check] The property chain ( bfo:bearer_of [ owl:inverseOf cco:is_about ] ) depends on the sosa:Observation being explicitly asserted as about the sosa:System.
preliminary_disposition: do not adopt directly in OWL; assess annotation/SHACL/rule
validated_basis: The chain bfo:bearer_of o cco:is_subject_of concludes in an Information Content Entity, whereas the SOSA-next relation ranges over OperatingConditions, Observation, or ObservationCollection. The chain does not express the source relation.

definition: Relation between a System and an ObservationCollection (or Observation) describing the capability of the system. A sensor or system may have more than one set of system capabilities with different validity contexts.
corrected_axiom: sosa:hasSystemCapability a owl:ObjectProperty ; rdfs:domain sosa:System ; rdfs:range [ a owl:Class ; owl:unionOf ( sosa:Observation sosa:ObservationCollection ) ] ; rdfs:comment "The workbook super-chain (bearer_of o inverse(is_about)) is not OWL 2 DL; the borne-capability aboutness constraint is moved to SHACL. external_notes: sosa:hasSystemCapability links a sosa:System to a sosa:ObservationCollection or sosa:Observation because system capabilities are expressed as observed or measurable values of properties such as accuracy, range, or resolution. This follows the SOSA pattern of representing system characteristics as observations, enabling capability descriptions to be queried and compared using the same mechanisms as observational data. [check] The property chain ( bfo:bearer_of [ owl:inverseOf cco:is_about ] ) depends on the sosa:Observation being explicitly asserted as about the sosa:System.
preliminary_disposition: do not adopt directly in OWL; assess annotation/SHACL/rule
validated_basis: The chain bfo:bearer_of o cco:is_subject_of concludes in an Information Content Entity, whereas the SOSA-next relation ranges over Observation or ObservationCollection. The chain does not express the source relation.

definition: Links a an observation collection or observation (typically about the system capabilities) or a property (typically about the system capabilities) to its validity context, described as an observation collection or observation (typically about the system environment)
corrected_axiom: sosa:hasValidityContext a owl:ObjectProperty ; rdfs:domain [ a owl:Class ; owl:unionOf ( sosa:Observation sosa:ObservationCollection sosa:Property ) ] ; rdfs:range [ a owl:Class ; owl:unionOf ( sosa:Observation sosa:ObservationCollection ) ] ; rdfs:comment "The workbook cell minted sosa:validityContextOf (an inverse partner absent from SOSA 2023 and every pinned source, coined inside the W3C sosa: namespace); it is dropped. An alignment must not mint IRIs in the aligned namespace; if an inverse is needed use ObjectInverseOf(sosa:hasValidityContext)."@en .
external_notes: sosa:hasValidityContext captures the conditionality of system capabilities and properties — a capability may only hold within specific environmental bounds. The domain is a union of sosa:Observation, sosa:ObservationCollection, and sosa:Property because validity contexts can qualify both capability descriptions and the properties themselves. The range is a sosa:ObservationCollection or sosa:Observation because environmental conditions are expressed as observed values in the SOSA pattern.

definition: Type of observation or observation collection that describe the conditions under which a system is expected to operate normally.
corrected_axiom: sosa:NormalOperatingConditions rdfs:subClassOf sosa:OperatingConditions .
external_notes: sosa:NormalOperatingConditions is a subclass of sosa:OperatingConditions because normal operating conditions are a specific type of operating conditions — those under which the system performs as designed. The subclass relationship captures the specialization without adding additional axioms, consistent with the simplified 2023 system capabilities module design.

definition: Type of observation or observation collection that describe operating conditions of systems. Sub-classes of this class explicit the desirability of the conditions. Three such sub-classes are provided as a basic classification: NormalOperatingConditions, SuboptimalOperatingConditions, and SurvivableConditions.
external_notes: sosa:OperatingConditions is modeled as a subclass of the union of sosa:Observation and sosa:ObservationCollection because operating conditions are expressed as observed values of environmental properties. This follows the SOSA pattern of using observations to represent system context, and allows operating conditions to be queried and compared using standard SOSA mechanisms. It is the superclass of sosa:NormalOperatingConditions, sosa:SuboptimalOperatingConditions, and sosa:SurvivableConditions.

definition: Type of observation or observation collection that describe the conditions under which a system is expected to operate sub-optimally. Results will still be reported but the performance of the sensor, in term of precision for example, will be impaired.
corrected_axiom: sosa:SuboptimalOperatingConditions rdfs:subClassOf sosa:OperatingConditions .
external_notes: sosa:SuboptimalOperatingConditions is a subclass of sosa:OperatingConditions because suboptimal operating conditions are a specific type of operating conditions — those under which the system continues to function but with degraded performance. The subclass relationship captures the specialization without adding additional axioms, consistent with the simplified 2023 system capabilities module design.

definition: Type of observation or observation collection that describe the conditions under which a system is expected to survive, that is to continue to exist in its current form, even if its future operations are impaired. A typical example is the temperature at which a sensor looses physical integrity and looses its shape. A system or sensor exposed to conditions outside of those reported by SurvivableConditions will no longer be serviceable.
corrected_axiom: sosa:SurvivableConditions rdfs:subClassOf sosa:OperatingConditions .
external_notes: sosa:SurvivableConditions is a subclass of sosa:OperatingConditions because survivable conditions are a specific type of operating conditions — those under which the system persists as a material entity even if operational capability is impaired or lost. The subclass relationship is consistent with the simplified 2023 module design. Note that survivability is distinct from normal or suboptimal operation: the system need not function, only continue to exist in its current form.

definition: links a Sample to a SampleRelationship
original_axiom:
sosa-rel:hasSampleRelationship schema:domainIncludes sosa:Sample .
sosa-rel:hasSampleRelationship schema:rangeIncludes sosa-rel:SampleRelationship .
corrected_axiom: sosa-rel:hasSampleRelationship a owl:ObjectProperty ; rdfs:domain sosa:Sample ; rdfs:range sosa-rel:SampleRelationship ; rdfs:comment "Declared as an object property with logical domain/range. The workbook's schema:domainIncludes / schema:rangeIncludes are annotation properties carrying no DL semantics (as the Reasoning states and native SOSA does); they are declared as owl:AnnotationProperty in this ontology so the merged graph stays in the OWL 2 DL profile."@en .
external_notes: sosa-rel:hasSampleRelationship uses schema:domainIncludes and schema:rangeIncludes rather than rdfs:domain and rdfs:range to avoid unintended type inferences. rdfs:domain and rdfs:range have formal entailments — any subject of this property would be inferred to be a sosa:Sample and any object inferred to be a sosa-rel:SampleRelationship, even in contexts where that inference is unwarranted. This is consistent with the lightweight SOSA axiomatization pattern, which uses schema:domainIncludes and schema:rangeIncludes throughout for the same reason.
